The construction company's negligence in leaving the worksite unsecured created a foreseeable risk of harm to the jogger. Under the rescue doctrine, a tortfeasor is also liable for injuries to a rescuer who attempts to save a victim from the peril created by the tortfeasor's negligence, provided the rescue attempt is foreseeable and not rash. The cyclist's rescue attempt was a foreseeable consequence of the jogger's peril, so the construction company will likely be held liable to the cyclist.
